newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish media boss on trial for rebel interview.
newsitem.headline: Turkish media boss on trial for rebel interview.

text.p: A Turkish court began the trial on Monday of a leading media tycoon and a newspaper editor for publishing an interview with Kurdish rebel leader Abdullah Ocalan, Anatolian news agency said.

Aydin Dogan, owner of Radikal newspaper and Yesim Denizel Beduk, the legally responsible editor, were charged under anti-terror laws for "publishing the statements of a terrorist organisation", Anatolian said.
Ocalan is believed to be based between Syria and Lebanon's eastern Bekaa valley.
The charge carries a fine of at least 50 billion Turkish lira ($394,000), the agency said.
Dogan has a controlling interest in Dogan Holding, through which he owns two other major national dailies, a television channel, insurance and leisure companies and an automotive distribution firm.

Radikal published the interview with Ocalan, leader of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) last December in which he called for talks with the Turkish authorities, but threatened attacks on major Turkish cities if his call was rejected.
The trial was adjourned to a later date to allow for files to be completed and the cross-examination of Dogan who was absent from the court.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in fighting between the Turkish security forces and the PKK who are fighting for independence or autonomy in the mainly Kurdish southeast of Turkey.
